summary:
STELLAR FRONTIER is an interactive space mission design and simulation game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the Space Mission Design Game challenge.

Players take the role of space mission planners, designing spacecraft, selecting launch vehicles, choosing propulsion and power systems, and managing scientific payloads, fuel, energy, materials, research, and mission budgets.

The simulator incorporates NASA GMAT R2026a astrodynamics resources, planetary constants, orbital mechanics, and real astronomical star catalog data. It calculates mission feasibility using spacecraft mass, propulsion performance, delta-v requirements, power generation, and operational costs.

Featuring an interactive 3D Solar System map, animated spacecraft missions, multiple mission phases, dynamic events, and a three-language interface (English, Azerbaijani, and Russian), STELLAR FRONTIER transforms complex space mission planning concepts into an accessible and engaging educational experience.

Its goal is to help users understand the engineering, scientific, and strategic challenges behind real-world space exploration
details:
STELLAR FRONTIER is a browser-based space mission design simulator that combines spacecraft engineering, orbital mechanics, resource management, and interactive 3D visualization.

The project provides a complete mission-planning experience through several interconnected systems:

Spacecraft Design: Players configure eight spacecraft module categories, including the frame, engine, fuel tank, solar panels, battery, communications, scientific instrument, and landing system.

Mission Economy: An integrated database provides four launch vehicle classes, seven destination profiles, four scientific payloads, propulsion options, and power systems. The game calculates launch expenses, propellant requirements, payload costs, power costs, and deep-space operational expenses in USD.

Physics and Feasibility: The simulation uses the rocket equation, delta-v requirements, gravitational parameters, orbital elements, and Hohmann transfer calculations. It evaluates spacecraft mass margins, propulsion limitations, fuel capacity, and power balance before launch.

Solar System Visualization: An interactive 3D star map displays planetary bodies, orbital paths, the asteroid belt, constellation lines, and mission trajectories. The 3D Mission Viewer illustrates spacecraft launch, stage separation, engine operation, atmospheric re-entry, parachute deployment, and landing.

Mission Progression: Players advance through five mission phases, encounter eight types of dynamic events, make scientific decisions, and receive a mission performance score based on objectives, science, budget, power, mass, and communications.

Accessibility: The entire game is contained in a standalone HTML file, supports English, Azerbaijani, and Russian, and automatically saves progress using browser local storage. A 2D fallback is available when WebGL is unsupported.

Development Tools: HTML5, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js, NASA GMAT R2026a reference data, and AI-assisted development tools (Claude and ChatGPT).

The project was developed to make the engineering and strategic challenges of interplanetary exploration understandable through hands-on experimentation. Its creative approach combines educational gameplay with engineering-inspired mission feasibility calculations and animated 3D space exploration.
